content.value_statement: Trading agents need consistent rules when working inside a market simulator. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured SMC workflow for Alpha Harness backtests.
actual_capabilities: Guides wake sessions with state review, market analysis, decision making, action, and alarm setup.
Applies Smart Money Concepts terms such as liquidity sweeps, fair value gaps, order blocks, and structure breaks.
Defines when to trade, watch, save a note, or take no action in the Alpha Harness simulator.
Provides fixed command patterns for creating setups, placing simulated orders, cancelling orders, and setting alarms.
Encourages recorded reasoning for each setup so backtest decisions can be reviewed later.
limitations: It is designed for Alpha Harness backtesting, not live trading execution.
It focuses on BTC/USDT examples and may need adaptation for other markets.
It depends on simulator commands and closed candle data supplied by the harness.
It does not prove that any trading method is profitable or suitable for real capital.

use_cases.title: Run Consistent Backtests
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable wake protocol so each simulated trading session follows the same analysis and risk rules.

use_cases.title: Build Trading Agents
use_cases.description: Give an AI agent a clear command vocabulary and decision framework for Alpha Harness experiments.

use_cases.title: Review SMC Decisions
use_cases.description: Compare setup reasoning, confidence, entry zones, stops, targets, and outcomes after simulated trades.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Wake Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SMC Harness workflow to orient, review current state, analyze BTC/USDT, and decide whether to trade, watch, note, or wait.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Potential Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this BTC/USDT setup with SMC criteria. Explain the higher timeframe bias, liquidity sweep, entry trigger, risk, target, and final decision.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Simulator Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this market analysis into Alpha Harness actions. Include the setup decision, simulated order plan, alarm levels, and reasoning to record.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Past Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review recent SMC setups and identify repeated decision errors, missed confirmations, risk issues, and rules that should change before the next session.

output_examples.input: Analyze BTC/USDT after a liquidity sweep and decide the next action.
output_examples.output: The higher timeframe bias is bullish, but the lower timeframe confirmation is incomplete. Decision: watch the setup and set an alarm near the entry zone.

output_examples.input: Review a potential long setup with a fair value gap and 2:1 risk reward.
output_examples.output: The setup meets the risk rule and has confluence from structure, sweep, and entry zone. Record the setup before placing any simulated order.

output_examples.input: Summarize what to do when an active order already exists.
output_examples.output: Check whether the original thesis is still valid. Keep the order if valid, cancel it if invalid, and avoid opening a second order.

best_practices: Create a setup and record reasoning before placing a simulated order.
Use alarms for key liquidity levels, fair value gaps, order blocks, and structure breaks.
Respect the one order limit and the maximum risk rule in every session.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for live financial advice or live order execution.
Do not place a trade when higher timeframe bias, trigger, or risk reward is unclear.
Do not skip notes, because missing reasoning makes backtest review less useful.

faq.question: What does this skill help an agent do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent analyze BTC/USDT in Alpha Harness and choose structured simulated trading actions.

faq.question: Is this skill for live trading?
faq.answer: No. It is written for a backtesting simulator and should not be used for live financial decisions.

faq.question: Which methodology does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Smart Money Concepts and ICT-style terms such as liquidity sweeps, fair value gaps, order blocks, and structure breaks.

faq.question: Can it place orders by itself?
faq.answer: It documents simulated Alpha Harness order workflows. Real execution depends on the host environment and user permissions.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review after a backtest?
faq.answer: Users should review setup reasoning, confidence, risk size, entries, stops, targets, and whether rules were followed.
